titel: Agents: set up the folder, rename, start
kurz: An agent works in a folder on this PC. So that the AMW can notify it, monitor it and show its usage, the AMW sets up this folder once.
brauchst: The folder the agent works in (usually the project folder).
The command line on the PC (`amw …`).

schritte.text: Run `amw einrichten agenten-ordner <folder> --projekt <project>`. The AMW adds its entries to the Claude Code settings in this folder and backs up the file first. After that, the agent's “State and usage” appears.
Settings › Agents shows folder, model, effort, permissions and first prompt. Change them there or with `amw agent profil <name> --ordner … --modell …`.
In the Overview click the agent › “Start / resume”. The AMW opens it in a new terminal tab.

werte: the project folder the agent works in
first sentence of a new session, e.g. “Read your messages and work through them.”
fehler: “No data yet” under State and usage
The folder is not set up yet (step 1), or the session was started before the setup. Restart it once.
The session is running but does not know its name. In the agent's window run `amw anmelden --von <name>`.
“… is logged in to another session”

A second Claude window uses the name of an agent that is already running in another window. The AMW does not accept commands under that name from there. Only if this really is the right agent: `amw anmelden --von <name> --ersetzen`.
The folder already belongs to another project
A folder belongs to exactly one project. Use a separate folder for a second project.
danach: Rename: `amw agent umbenennen <old> <new>`. The old name stays valid as a second name, so older messages and commands keep working.
`amw einrichten agenten-ordner <folder> --entfernen` removes what the AMW added to the folder.
fragen: Why can't I rename in the Workbench?
The name is used in start scripts and running sessions on this PC. The command line changes everything in one place without a running session losing its name.
How do I start an agent by hand – for example after restarting the PC?

⋯ on the agent › “Start command …” (or Settings › Agents › “Start command to copy”). It lists folder, extra folders, model, effort, permissions and the last session, followed by two ready lines: “Resume” (last session) and “Start fresh” – for PowerShell or the command prompt. “Copy”, paste into a terminal, Enter. This is exactly how AMW starts the agent itself.
How much does an agent use per task?

Click the agent › Overview › “Usage per task”: the median of the last ten finished tasks, the model and effort that are set, the task in progress so far and the amount for each task. A task's window shows its value under “Usage”; on the command line see `amw aufgabe zeige <nr>` and `amw agent profil <name>`. It counts the dollar equivalent Claude Code reports per session – also on a subscription, where nothing is paid extra. Per task it is approximated: what was used between start and finish counts towards the task the agent started last – a task that is waiting at that moment comes second. The task's window also shows the times: active and waiting – before the start, while building by reason (review, run, you …) and after hand-in until delivery. Runs outside a session (e.g. `claude -p`) are added by the agent with `amw kosten erfassen --aufgabe <nr> --json <file>`; what is not measured is listed under “Not measured”. All tasks at once: `amw messung`; this week against the week before: `amw messung --vergleich`. One gap is listed for every task: what the lead does for it (reviewing, planning) is not counted – so “with gaps” only counts tasks where something else is missing too. The numbers help when setting model and effort in the profile; they apply from the next start.
What do the agents spend their money on?

Operations › “Where the money goes” (on the PC) or `amw verbrauch pareto --tage 7`: each cost increase of a session belongs to the wake-ups in the same period – such as “Run is due”, review request, answer, order –; without a wake-up it counts as own work. The most expensive comes first, with share, number of wake-ups and cost per wake-up. “Avoidable” means the agent did not have to do anything for it. This shows which wake-ups are most worth switching off.
Which model and effort does AMW recommend?

When creating a task, the lead gives it a size and a type: `amw aufgabe neu … --groesse S|M|L|XL --art text|mechanisch|fehlersuche|oberflaeche|sicherheit|konzept` (later with `amw aufgabe aendern <nr>`). From that AMW suggests model and effort – using a table per project (Settings › Project › “Recommended model · effort”). The starting values are an assumption; next to the suggestion on the task you see what finished tasks of the same type and size actually used and how often their review was red. Use that to adjust the table. The agent shows the recommendation from its recent tasks; “Apply to profile” sets it. AMW changes nothing by itself and restarts no one: the profile applies from the next start.
May the lead change an agent's profile while I am away from the PC?

Yes, if you told them to: the lead records your words and changes the profile with `amw agent profil <agent> --ordner … --wort W<nr>` – also through the file exchange. The words must be from this project and at most 24 hours old. It only covers profile fields such as folder, extra folders, model and effort; the role and the lead's own permissions or remote control are changed only by the developer at the PC. Every change appears in the history as old → new, and you get an info about it.
What are work places?

For agents that work without a window of their own (`claude -p`), AMW keeps work places: per place its own clone of the project (nothing is shared with your project folder) and next to it its own data folder with its own database, settings and port. Whatever runs there never reaches the real database. Only you decide where the places are and how many there are: `amw projekt einstellen platz_wurzel=<folder> --von Entwickler` and `amw projekt einstellen plaetze=2 --von Entwickler`. The folder must not be inside the project folder. Without this setting (default 0 places) nothing changes. `amw platz liste` shows them, `amw platz vorbereiten 1` brings place 1 to the state of main, `amw platz zuruecksetzen 1` cleans it again – also after an abort. Nothing is deleted: leftovers (unsaved changes as a patch, commits, foreign files, the data folder) move to the folder `_archiv` next to the places; once the package is finished, `amw platz aufraeumen` moves them to `_loeschen`. Only you empty that folder – `amw platz liste` shows how much is in it.
How does AMW check the work of an agent at a work place?

It does not trust the agent's report but runs the acceptance itself – in the place, with its data and port, with a time limit; if a test hangs, AMW ends it together with everything it started. Before building, the acceptance must be red, otherwise it checks nothing. Afterwards AMW checks that only the planned areas changed and no locked path: delivery, rights, hooks, `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, acceptance and test scripts, test configuration – test files only for the package type “test-schreiben”, and then the new test must be red against the old state. Without work places set up, none of this happens.
Who may give the merge OK?

The lead and you – and the reviewer who set the latest check of a task to green: `amw freigabe merge A12`. This way an agent who only reviews can approve without full lead rights. An exception from the full test run is still recorded only by the lead and you.
Why does a command from my development folder refuse the database?

The database belongs to the AMW service. If a command runs with code from another folder (development or check folder) and reaches this database through the settings, it may only read – not change it and not lift it to a new schema. Work there with your own file: `AMW_DB=<own file>`. Run commands for real work from the AMW folder.
When does AMW start a package at a work place – and when not?

Before every start it asks the guard. It does not start when the acceptance command or the areas are missing (rule 1), the areas overlap with a running package (2), the package needs the graphics card, the screen or a lot of computing power (3), all places are taken (4), the areas contain locked paths (5), the acceptance is already green before building (6), maintenance mode is on (7), the account's weekly limit is at 80 % or more (8), two runs in a row ended unclear or aborted (9 – pause) or no places are set up (10). Each reason is logged with its number: `amw waechter protokoll`. A delivery of AMW switches on maintenance mode and waits until running packages end. The lead or you lift maintenance mode and pause: `amw waechter weiter`.
